lede: I'm donxy. I work on visible–thermal multimodal object detection, and the question I keep coming back to is: when one modality degrades, goes missing, or turns unreliable, how does a fusion detector stay robust? This page is the front door to three lines I maintain over the long term — paper deep reads, figure teardowns, and autonomous-driving notes — each with its own site, all continuously updated.

rgbt_card1_p: Structured notes on {{PAPERS_TOTAL}} RGBT object-detection papers (core {{PAPERS_CORE}} / appendix {{PAPERS_APPENDIX}}): organized by technical route, with depth badges (abstract-level / full-text deep read), tag filtering, and a dataset quick reference. Deep-read entries include the main framework figure and a six-section structured note.
rgbt_card2_p: A general-purpose RGBT object-detection library for the whole field: the catalogue, references, and BibTeX are generated from papers.csv as the single source of truth, with consistency validation — every note on the site traces back to a record in this library.
rgbt_wide_h3: Organized by fusion level, not stacked by year
rgbt_wide_p: The whole literature is organized along the level at which fusion happens — the “metro map” behind the notes site: each route forms its own line, so which lines are crowded and which are still empty is visible at a glance. Station counts are the paper counts at that level.
route_na: Plus {{NA_COUNT}} survey & cross-level works not counted in the level lines
title: donxy — Research Notes & Visual Teardowns
visual_card1_p: Issue by issue, a teardown of the figure design in top-conference and top-journal papers: color systems, layout composition, graphic components, and where the polish comes from — color values sampled from the original figures. Each issue ships with style-reproduction prompts ready for AI image generation, building four libraries: palettes, layouts, components, and prompts.
visual_card2_p: Each issue looks only at the first three figures of one paper: get the originals, zoom in and crop, then talk design. Measured color values and dimensions are labelled as measured; design intent is labelled as inferred — guesses never pose as facts, the same discipline as the deep-read notes.
